arms.predicted: Pareto density for Llama-3.1-8B at rate=50 will be higher than Qwen3-14B's 4.5% (predicted range 6-12%). Exhaustive HV will differ from Qwen's 5.857e10 due to higher throughput ceiling (31.67 rps vs ~26 rps for Qwen).
arms.observed: Llama density: 96/1800 = 5.33%. Exhaustive HV: 7.754e10. Both higher than Qwen (4.5%, 5.857e10) as predicted. However density 5.33% is below the predicted range of 6-12%. The higher throughput ceiling drives higher HV (32% larger than Qwen's), confirming the architecture difference. Diagnostic: density lower than predicted range suggests Llama's higher rps ceiling concentrates the Pareto front — mid-range rps configs are dominated out by high-throughput Llama configs more than expected.
arms.diagnostic_note: Density 5.33% is directionally correct (> 4.5%) but below predicted range (6-12%). The weaker KV stress interaction correctly predicts fewer dominated configs, but Llama's higher throughput ceiling eliminates mid-range configs from the Pareto front, partially offsetting the density gain.

arms.predicted: NSGA-II on Llama-3.1-8B reaches 95% of exhaustive HV before random search (portability confirmed). Convergence gap will be smaller than Qwen's 91-eval gap (predicted 40-70 evals). NSGA-II final HV >= 97% of exhaustive.
arms.observed: NSGA-II checkpoints (% of exhaustive HV 7.754e10): eval=40: 89.01%, eval=80: 90.06%, eval=120: 95.87%, eval=160: 99.67%, eval=200: 99.87%. NSGA-II reaches 95% at interpolated eval ~114. Random search reaches 95% at interpolated eval ~91. Convergence gap at 95% threshold: NSGA-II is 22.9 evals SLOWER than random (gap = -22.9 evals, random wins). Final HV: NSGA-II 99.87% vs random 98.21%, NSGA-II advantage preserved at final eval.
arms.diagnostic_note: NSGA-II portability (same interaction structure) is confirmed — it still finds a high-quality Pareto front (99.87% final HV). But at 5.33% density, random search is faster to the 95% threshold (by 22.9 evals) because uniform sampling hits Pareto-optimal configs with high probability at this density. The predicted gap of 40-70 evals is wrong in direction (NSGA-II is slower, not faster, at the 95% threshold). NSGA-II retains final HV advantage (1.66pp), confirming the algorithm correctly exploits structure but density has shifted the breakeven point past 5.33%.

arms.predicted: Random search reaches 95% of exhaustive HV within 200 evals. Final HV >= 95% of exhaustive, higher than Qwen random at rate=50.
arms.observed: Random search checkpoints: eval=40: 86.62%, eval=80: 94.54%, eval=120: 96.20%, eval=160: 96.45%, eval=200: 98.21%. Reaches 95% at interpolated eval ~91 (within budget). Final HV 7.615e10 = 98.21% of exhaustive. Comparison: Llama random 98.21% > Qwen random in iter-7 (97.56%), confirming higher random coverage for higher-density frontier.
arms.diagnostic_note: Random search is highly effective at 5.33% density. With 200 evals and 5.33% density, expected Pareto hits ~10.7, enough for >95% HV coverage. The 98.21% final HV (vs 95% threshold) confirms the density prediction drives random search performance above expectations.

arms.predicted: Re-running NSGA-II and random on Qwen3-14B reproduces iter-5's convergence gap within 10 evals (91 ± 10). Infrastructure validation: same BLIS binary, same model config.
arms.observed: Qwen NSGA-II (iter-7): eval=40: 87.40%, eval=80: 89.67%, eval=120: 95.97%, eval=160: 99.20%, eval=200: 99.59%. Reaches 95% at ~eval 114. Qwen Random (iter-7): eval=40: 86.21%, eval=80: 93.37%, eval=120: 95.07%, eval=160: 95.33%, eval=200: 97.56%. Reaches 95% at ~eval 118. Within-iter-7 gap: 4.6 evals (NSGA-II barely faster). Infrastructure check: NSGA-II eval=40 = 87.40% matches iter-5 exactly (87.4%), confirming identical initial population, BLIS binary unchanged, Qwen model config unchanged. Gap difference from iter-5 (~91 evals): 86.5 evals outside 10-eval tolerance, caused by different offspring generation strategy in iter-7 blis_common.py (single vs paired offspring per parent selection).
arms.diagnostic_note: Infrastructure validation PASSES (eval=40 match 87.4% confirms same initial population, same BLIS binary, same Qwen config). Gap reproduction FAILS because iter-7 blis_common.py generates one offspring per tournament vs iter-5's paired offspring per parent pair — different RNG consumption after eval=40. The within-iter-7 comparison (Qwen gap 4.6 vs Llama gap -22.9) is valid for cross-model comparison since both use the same implementation. Qwen iter-5 gap not reproducible due to implementation change, but direction (Llama gap < Qwen gap) is preserved.

discrepancy_analysis: The main discrepancy is in h-main: random search reaches 95% of exhaustive HV BEFORE NSGA-II for Llama-3.1-8B (contrary to the portability prediction). This occurs because Llama's 5.33% Pareto density is above the ~5% threshold where NSGA-II's convergence speed advantage disappears. At 5.33% density with 200/1800 = 11.1% coverage, random expects ~10.7 Pareto hits — sufficient to reach 95% HV before NSGA-II's crossover operator fully exploits the landscape structure. NSGA-II retains a final HV advantage (99.87% vs 98.21%), confirming the algorithm still finds a better coverage given sufficient budget. The h-ablation gap discrepancy (86.5 evals vs 91-eval prediction) is explained by implementation differences between iter-5 and iter-7, not a BLIS change. The within-iter-7 cross-model comparison remains valid.
